claim: `Build::promote` overwrites `refs[R]` without emitting a committed-to-committed repoint event, so the previously committed manifest and its uniquely owned blobs remain pinned forever.
A crash or exception after `republishRef` promotes the destination ref but before it drops the source ref causes a retry to mint a fresh manifest and leak the first committed destination manifest.
`Build::abandon` retires `build_seq` before appending the precommit-removal event, allowing GC precommit reclamation to race the abandonment removal.

The committed read pipeline discards the resolved manifest and ref after planning a deferred blob GET, so dropping the ref and completing GC can make the later GET fail with `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` during a long read.
`readManifest` caches bytes fetched at GET token `Tg` under the preceding HEAD token `Th`, rather than under the token of the object whose bytes were decoded.
The `allow_stale` resolve path can use a ref dropped up to the 200 ms cache TTL ago, but no assertion enforces that `shard_decode_cache_ttl_ms` is shorter than GC condemn-to-graduate latency.

A manifest-cache hit still performs a `HEAD`; this deliberate fail-closed tradeoff removes the GET and decode but not the round trip, and a blob-backed open costs at least two `HEAD`s, up to two control `GET`s, and one blob `GET`.
After a lost-ACK `dropRef` CAS, replaying the closure can throw `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` even though the ref removal already committed; conditional-write conflicts should reconcile the post-state instead.
A lost-ACK publish or promote can replay its closure and append a duplicate journal event, producing journal bloat even though set-based GC keeps blob in-degree semantically correct.
The flat-combining write queue can block every writer queued on one `(namespace, shard)` behind a stalled leader, and a transient leader failure can fail the entire carved batch.

Interrupted multipart uploads and lost-ACK `stageManifest` operations can leave storage debris that depends on the orphan-manifest sweep and an S3 `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` lifecycle rule for reclamation.

The CAS write path maps ambiguous conditional-write outcomes to failure rather than false success, so non-precondition errors propagate and no object is treated as committed unless the write is known to have landed.

A regular GC round acquires a lease, computes a heartbeat floor, folds shard journals into attempt artifacts, performs only previously published `delete_pending` deletes, publishes retired-list runs, and advances all state with one `gc/state` CAS.
`computeHeartbeatFloor` treats transient or unreadable mounts as live and holds `min_ack` down; only causally dead mounts are excluded, so injected S3 faults cannot raise the graduation floor.

`deleteExact` propagates transient, throttle, and authentication errors instead of forgetting the entry, while `TokenMismatch` and `NotFound` remain terminal outcomes for the exact-token deletion attempt.
A persistent clamp on one GC shard leaves `suppress_destructive` set for every pass and halts blob and manifest deletion across the entire pool.
A referenced-but-missing or corrupt GC run, retired list, or adopted fold seal raises `CORRUPTED_DATA` and refuses the GC round until an operator performs GC rebuild.

If a lost acknowledgment follows a committed GC `gc/state` CAS, the retry reports `ABORTED`, while the next round reads the already advanced state and treats the earlier exact-token deletes as terminal and safe.
GC streams the three-cursor merge but accumulates the round's `std::vector<BlobDelta>` in memory, so a large mass-drop delta can cause an OOM and repeated lack of progress for that shard.
A single CAS `RootShard` is a per-shard linearizable register and journal, while multi-shard operations such as `RENAME` are not transactional and provide no cross-shard serializability guarantee.
CAS blobs and manifests are immutable, content-addressed, write-once objects, and GC is required to preserve no dangle, no returned token, and over-count rather than under-count.
`republishRef` performs a create-destination-shard CAS followed by a drop-source-shard CAS, so a concurrent reader can observe both names or neither during the cross-shard window.

The `allow_stale` read mode can return a cached shard value up to approximately 200 ms old, whereas force-fresh reads request the current value subject to backend consistency and writer-fencing limits.

A writer paused beyond its mount lease can pass `mayMutate`, be paused before `casPut`, and then commit a shard mutation after another incarnation has claimed the mount because the shard CAS checks only a content token, not `writer_epoch`.
A VM clone or snapshot restore can duplicate `server_uuid` and create a dual-writer window until the original mount's next renewal detects the superseded `writer_epoch`.
Mount reclamation uses wall-clock lease expiry while the local write fence uses boot-clock time, so sufficient clock skew can let one server reclaim a lease that another still believes it holds.

The security perimeter of a CAS pool is the S3 bucket credential: pool members sharing it can read and write blobs, refs, manifests, GC state, pool metadata, and mount objects, with no intra-pool authorization.
Pool-global deduplication uses non-cryptographic `CityHash128` content keys without normal read-time payload rehashing, so a collision can poison a blob across tables or tenants that share a pool.
HEAD-first deduplication makes an existing content key observably cheaper to write, allowing an inserter to test whether candidate content already exists anywhere in a pool shared across namespaces.

`SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` reconstructs per-shard fold cursors and blob in-degree from owner shards and journals, and its baseline guard raises `CORRUPTED_DATA` when trimmed history cannot be accounted for.

The later GCR-1 re-triage concluded that `rebuildBaseline` computes the mount-lease ack-floor and installs `gc/state` with a fail-closed CAS, so floor-gated graduation protects post-snapshot writer objects without refusing rebuild while writers are mounted.
The re-triage records that shard-incarnation state carries `writer_epoch`, fencing builds from superseded mount incarnations before they mutate a shard.
`clampBefore` emits a `clamped` event row containing the clamped key and shard, providing operator visibility into GC clamp conditions.
The re-triage records that conditional-write conflict paths reconcile by reading post-state and adopt the other party's result instead of blindly replaying the closure.
Before the P3-B1 fix, a new GC leader set `i_am_leader` only after `runRoundLogged` returned, leaving its first long fold without heartbeat protection and allowing deterministic lease stealing.
The P3-B1 fix invokes an `on_lease_acquired` hook immediately after `acquireOrRenewLease`, sets `i_am_leader`, and pulses the heartbeat before folding begins.

The remaining P3-B1 RFC residuals are to verify AWS SDK region-redirect retry behavior when `region` is `aws-global` and to verify retry semantics of `IObjectStorage::copyObjectConditional` used by `promoteStaged`.
The user-facing `cas-inspect` JSON key `ns` was renamed to `namespace`, while persisted wire-format `ns` keys remain unchanged.
Persisted `ManifestRef` fields use the wire keys `me` for `writer_epoch`, `mb` for `build_sequence`, and `mo` for `manifest_ordinal`; no user-facing copy of these keys was found.
Persisted `BlobRef` fields use `ha` for the hash algorithm and `h` for the digest hex, and the searched user-facing tools contain no `p` JSON/output key.
The S44 smoke run applied 54 mutations across six drop/recreate cycles with no mutation errors beyond the expected drop-window `UNKNOWN_TABLE` exceptions.
The S44 smoke run's recreate latency stayed stable at 2.349 seconds in the first half and 2.347 seconds in the second half.
The S44 smoke run ended with `CasRefApplyPoisoned=0`, `CasRefRecoveryStreamHole=0`, and `fsck --detail` reporting `dangling=0`.
S44's concurrent mutation-stream SQL proxy confirms the tested `writeFile` call path but does not establish that it is fully faithful to a raw namespace-file reader or writer.

`ca-drop-member` refuses a victim whose mount lease is alive or contended; with `mount_lease_ttl_ms=30000` and `mount_renew_period=10000`, the decommission path must wait for lease expiry because it has no `FORCE` variant.
A `ReplicatedMergeTree` table is materialized per replica, so a decommission test must create the table on the victim replica to create that replica's local namespace.
A `ReplicatedMergeTree` `DROP` is per replica rather than automatically cluster-wide, so hidden `Removing` catalog entries require dropping the table on both replicas before killing the victim.
The decommission sweep retains manifests when epoch 1's closing seal is not consumed, leaving them to normal GC; this can produce nonzero `unreachable` with `dangling=0` and no data loss.

The soak harness watched the removed `CasRefApplyPoisoned` profile event even though production had renamed it to `CasRefNeedsRecovery`, causing phase-3 preflight to abort until the watch list was updated.
`gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget` defaults to 5000 manifest deletions per GC round, and the value `0` means unbounded cleanup.
When `gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget` is exhausted, manifest bodies nominated but declined in that round are not re-derived by later rounds, creating an unbounded unreachable-manifest leak.
The manifest orphan sweep lists at most 1000 keys and deletes at most 100 keys per round, so it cannot promptly drain a large budget-induced manifest-deletion debt.
With the default cleanup budget, one T6b run accumulated 112518 `skipped_budget` nominations and ended with 110218 unreachable objects after 73 rounds.
With `gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget=0`, a T6b run had zero `skipped_budget` entries and both recovery and final convergence reached `unreachable=0`, `dangling=0`, and `stale_edge=0`.
The T6b evidence led to the decision to remove `gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget` entirely, including its disabled value `0`, rather than retain the cap.
During the recorded interval, no `ch1` or `ch2` ref deletes occurred, while all-time `ch2` ref-object deletes also remained zero.
The recorded `ch2` activity included 45 touches in the `ch1` namespace under the `cas/manifests` prefix.
Across the stale-edge sample from rounds 109 through 254, `stale_edge` remained 15 and `unreachable` remained 15 while `pending_gc` and `awaiting_gc` remained zero for the constant keyset `c82df19e`.
Setting `metadata_type` to `cas` makes an object-storage disk content-addressed, shares identical content across parts or tables, and enables background reclamation after references disappear.
A CAS disk requires `server_root_id`; each replica sharing an endpoint must use a distinct owned subtree, and omitting the key is a startup error.

`scratch_path` is a server-local filesystem directory for staging write-buffer data, defaults to `<clickhouse-path>/disks/<disk_name>/cas_scratch/`, and a relative override is anchored to the server data path.
`staging_backend` accepts `local` or `s3`; `local` is the default and stages in-flight part data locally, while `s3` enables S3-native staging.
`blob_hash` accepts `cityhash128` or `sha256`, and the pool records the choice so reopening with a disagreement fails closed.
`blob_hash_allow_new` defaults to `false` and must be enabled to admit a new blob-hash algorithm into an existing pool's recorded algorithm set.
`gc_enabled` defaults to `true`, and `gc_interval_sec` defaults to 60 seconds with a minimum value of 1 second.
`gc_shards` defaults to 1, must be at least 1, and is creation-time-only because persisted GC state is authoritative on reopen.
`deduplication_cache_bytes` defaults to 64 MiB, and `deduplication_head_first_min_bytes` defaults to 1 MiB with `0` disabling the pre-upload `HEAD`.
`gc_snapshot_generations_to_keep` defaults to 3, while `manifest_sweep_list_budget_keys` and `manifest_sweep_delete_budget_keys` default to 1000 and 100 per round respectively.

On generation-token backends, `gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes` defaults to 1 GiB and conditional writes larger than that are rejected with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; the limit is irrelevant to ETag-based AWS S3 backends.

`part_folder_cache_bytes` defaults to 64 MiB and `0` disables retention as a supported permanent operational configuration; `part_folder_cache_max_entries` defaults to 10000 and `part_folder_cache_max_entry_bytes` defaults to 16 MiB.
`part_folder_validate` defaults to `always`, also accepts `never` or `age <seconds>`, and controls how often a `ForceFresh` read re-proves a cached manifest body with `HEAD`.
`manifest_decode_cache_bytes` defaults to 128 MiB, and `0` disables decoded-manifest caching.
`gc_meta_pool_size` defaults to 16 and bounds the thread pool used for GC freshness-metadata writes during condemn, spare, and delete operations.
